I added `tests/public/isIgnored.test.ts`, and it type-checks with no errors.

**Where the test keys come from:** `spec.md` has no tagged scenarios. Its one sentence says the function returns "whether git ignores the file", so git's own `.gitignore` rules define the answer. I treated that as a single scenario and keyed every test `[happy-1]`. A comment at the top of the file says so. If you add tagged scenarios to the spec, the test names need re-keying to match.

**What the tests cover:**
- **Basics:** an empty `.gitignore`, blank lines and `#` comments, and `\#` / `\!` escapes.
- **Patterns without a slash:** they match a file or directory at any depth.
- **A trailing `/`:** it matches directories only.
- **A leading or middle `/`:** it ties the pattern to the root.
- **Wildcards:** `*` and `?` don't cross a `/`, and a `[0-9]` set matches one character.
- **`**`:** used at the start, at the end, and in the middle.
- **Negation with `!`:**
  - the last matching line wins;
  - a file can't be brought back if its parent directory is excluded;
  - excluding `logs/*` does let a file in it be brought back;
  - the git docs' "exclude everything except `foo/bar`" example.
- **Trailing spaces:** ignored unless escaped.

**Checks:**
- **Types:** I ran `tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit`, which does the same type check as `npm run build`. I didn't run `npm run build` itself because it writes compiled `.js` files into `src/`.
- **Expected answers:** I compared all 52 assertions against real git 2.54 (`git check-ignore --no-index`) in throwaway repos in the scratchpad. All 52 matched.
- **Test run:** I haven't run the tests. They will fail until `isIgnored` is implemented.

19 tests, in 1 file.
